newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.2 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.2 pct in June.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said on Wednesday its median Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent in June after gaining 0.3 percent in May.

The Cleveland Fed's median CPI is a mesure of core inflation which excludes items that markedly depart from the median performance of most items. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)'s core CPI only excludes food and energy prices.
The median CPI rose at annualized rate of 2.8 percent in June and was also up 2.8 percent year-over-year in June vs. up 2.7 percent year-over-year in May.
Earlier, the BLS said the U.S. CPI and core CPI both inched up 0.1 percent in June. Year/over/year, CPI and core CPI were up 2.3 percent and they 2.5 percent, respectively.
